answer: Admit a new identity only when it presents credentials from at least three unrelated issuers, such as a work platform, a payment provider, and a community registry, passing a quorum check. No single issuer can mint identities alone, so an attacker must forge, buy, or bribe standing across several independent systems, multiplying cost and leaving a revocation trail in each. Count distinct roots in a grove, not shoots: if any issuer revokes, quorum is lost and the identity is suspended, as a harbor trusts only ships sighted by lighthouses. One lotus petal proves nothing; the root system does.
